spec: CONTROL.md §6.3, A busy window is asked twice
note: Whether a machine waits a moment for a window's hooks before it routes a message for it. `look` is why the window's own inbox was no way in (`busy`: its registry row says a turn is running; any other reason; or null: it could be written to, or was never looked at because a rung above took the message, which is where a window that is mid-turn by its hooks goes). `hooks_heard`: this session's hooks have reported to the machine at all. `has_copy`: the session's messages go to a copy, so the window looked at is the copy's. `asked_before`: this message has waited once already. `expect` is `waits` (for the hooks to say a turn began, a short while: two seconds in the reference daemon; then the message is routed again) or `routes` (at once, as the ladder says).

cases.name: the first moments of a turn typed in the window: the row says busy, the hooks' report is on its way
it waited, and is looked at again: whatever the window says now is the answer
a busy window whose hooks have never reported here: they never will
the busy window is the copy's, and the turn rung reads the session the message names
an idle window that can be written to
a process that is not a window
